<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, skip this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to EnterPlanMode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke Skill tool" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to EnterPlanMode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke Skill tool" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke Skill tool" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.


</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 16:36:59 2026 +0100

    test(versioncheck): pin the auto-updater's shell command to literals
    
    The `sh -c` in realRunInstaller is a considered exception to "never put a
    dynamic value on a shell line", not an oversight: updateCommand returns one
    of five compile-time literals, the binary's path and version choose between
    them rather than appearing inside them, and the shell is load-bearing for
    the fallback, which is a pipeline (`curl … | bash`). Rewriting that as argv
    means re-implementing the pipe, which is more moving parts than the risk it
    removes.
    
    That reasoning holds only while the literals stay literal, and the tempting
    next change is the one that breaks it — interpolating the channel, the
    version, or the Scoop app name into the command, which would look entirely
    reasonable in review. So enforce it: drive every install manager and
    channel with adversarial exec paths and versions, and fail when the result
    is not one of the known strings.
    
    The adversarial inputs are not a claim that an attacker controls them. They
    are there so a future interpolation surfaces as a failing test rather than
    as a quoting question nobody thinks to ask.

+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck_test.go
@@ -800,3 +800,65 @@ func TestCheckAndNotify_FetchFailureUpdatesCacheToPreventRetry(t *testing.T) {
 		t.Errorf("cache LastCheckTime not updated after fetch failure: %v", cache.LastCheckTime)
 	}
 }
+
+// knownUpdateCommands is every string updateCommand may return. It is a closed
+// set on purpose: realRunInstaller hands the result to `sh -c` (or, on the
+// currently unreachable Windows branch, to `cmd /C`), and that is only
+// defensible while nothing runtime-derived reaches the string.
+var knownUpdateCommands = map[string]struct{}{
+	"brew upgrade --yes entire":         {},
+	"brew upgrade --yes entire@nightly": {},
+	"mise upgrade entire":               {},
+	"scoop update entire/entire":        {},
+	`cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install entire/entire && scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop reset entire"`: {},
+	"curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash":                                                  {},
+	"curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly":                          {},
+}
+
+// TestUpdateCommandIsAlwaysALiteral is the guard behind realRunInstaller's
+// decision to keep `sh -c`.
+//
+// The version string and the executable path are the only inputs, and today
+// they only select among fixed commands. Interpolating either into the command
+// — the channel into a URL, the Scoop app name into a package spec — is the
+// change that turns a shell invocation of a constant into a shell invocation of
+// a runtime value, and it would look entirely reasonable in review. The
+// adversarial cases below are not a claim that an attacker controls these
+// inputs; they are there so that a future interpolation shows up as a failing
+// test rather than as a quoting question nobody asks.
+func TestUpdateCommandIsAlwaysALiteral(t *testing.T) {
+	versions := []string{
+		"1.0.0",
+		"1.0.1-nightly.202604101200.abc1234",
+		"",
+		"1.0.0; touch /tmp/pwned",
+		"$(touch /tmp/pwned)",
+		"1.0.0-nightly.`id`",
+	}
+	execPaths := []string{
+		"/opt/homebrew/bin/entire",
+		"/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/entire",
+		"/home/user/.local/share/mise/installs/entire/1.0.0/bin/entire",
+		scoopExecutablePath,
+		scoopEntireExecutablePath,
+		plainBinPath,
+		"/home/user/scoop/apps/cli; touch \\x2ftmp\\x2fpwned/current/entire.exe",
+		"/home/user/scoop/apps/$(id)/current/entire.exe",
+	}
+
+	for _, version := range versions {
+		for _, path := range execPaths {
+			original := executablePath
+			executablePath = func() (string, error) { return path, nil }
+			got := updateCommand(version)
+			executablePath = original
+
+			if _, known := knownUpdateCommands[got]; !known {
+				t.Errorf("updateCommand(%q) with exec path %q = %q, which is not one of the known literals.\n"+
+					"realRunInstaller passes this to `sh -c`, which is only safe while the command is a "+
+					"compile-time constant. A command that needs a runtime value must be built and run as "+
+					"argv instead of being added to knownUpdateCommands.", version, path, got)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}

is allowed because there is no dynamic value in it: on unix
`UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` returns one of five compile-time literals, and
the binary's path and version choose *between* them and never appear *in* them —
while the shell is load-bearing for the fallback, which is a pipeline
(`curl … | bash`). The tempting next change is exactly the one that breaks this:
interpolating a channel or a version into the command.
`TestUpdateCommandIsAlwaysALiteral` (in `versioncheck_unix_test.go`) drives every
unix install manager and channel with adversarial paths and versions and fails
when the result is not a known string. A command that genuinely needs a runtime
value must be built and run as argv, not added to that set.

Windows is deliberately outside that invariant rather than an exception to it:
`fallbackInstallCommand` there interpolates the running binary's directory into
`-InstallDir`, and it is safe to because Windows never *runs* the command —
`realRunInstaller` is unimplemented there, so the string is only ever printed
for the user to paste.
'''
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
PY

Rebase is complete — all 7 commits applied onto `78a655db4`, lint clean, tests passing.

Two conflicts, both caused by upstream refactors landing under the incoming commits:

**1. `cmd/entire/cli/doctor_test.go`** (commit: *confine git hook installation to a rooted hooks directory*)

Two disjoint test suites collided at the same file position — HEAD's `scanForSymlinkedComponent` / `componentHasExpectedShape` / agent-dir tests, and the incoming `checkGitHookSymlinks` tests. Kept both in full; nothing was dropped.

**2. `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/`** (commit: *pin the auto-updater's shell command to literals*)

Upstream had since split `realRunInstaller` and the install probes into `_unix.go` / `_windows.go`, and made the **Windows** fallback deliberately interpolate the install dir into `-InstallDir`. That invalidates the incoming commit as written — its `TestUpdateCommandIsAlwaysALiteral` would fail on Windows, and it called a now-renamed `updateCommand`. I preserved the commit's intent, rescoped to where the invariant actually holds:

- Rationale comment → `autoupdate_unix.go`'s `realRunInstaller` (where the `sh -c` now lives).
- "Every command here is a literal" note → `versioncheck_unix.go`.
- Test → moved to `versioncheck_unix_test.go`, using `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary`, unix literals only, with unix-shaped adversarial exec paths replacing the Scoop ones.
- CLAUDE.md → updated to name the current symbol and to state explicitly that Windows is *outside* the invariant rather than an exception to it (safe because `realRunInstaller` is unimplemented there, so the string is only printed).

Verified: `go build ./...` and `GOOS=windows go build ./...` both clean, `versioncheck`/`strategy`/`osroot` pass, `mise run lint` reports 0 issues.

One note on the test run: `./cmd/entire/cli/` initially showed 27 failures, all from your global `core.hooksPath = ~/.git-hooks` leaking into test repos (the known pre-existing issue). Re-running with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null` gives `ok` — so nothing there is from the rebase.

Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 16:26:25 2026 +0100

    fix(explain): gate external summary-provider discovery on external_agents
    
    summary_generation.provider is honored from the COMMITTED
    .entire/settings.json, and discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing resolved an
    unregistered name by executing entire-agent-<name>'s info subcommand. One
    line in a pull request was therefore enough to run a binary of the
    author's choosing on everyone who pulled it and ran `entire explain` — no
    prompt, no grant, and never consulting enforceExternalAgentsTrust.
    
    Resolving by name rather than sweeping $PATH bounds that to one binary; it
    does not make it zero. Gate the lookup on settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled.
    
    The check sits after the already-registered early return, so it lands only
    on the external case: a committed "provider": "claude-code" keeps working
    with external agents off, which is the ordinary configuration and has
    nothing to do with plugins.
    
    When the gate declines, the resulting error gains a line naming the grant.
    "unknown summary provider" about a plugin that is plainly installed is not
    something a user can act on.
    
    Two existing tests granted external_agents from the committed project
    file, which the trust gate has never honored — they only passed because
    this path bypassed it. Both now grant it from the untracked local layer.
    
    Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit f237f08b82110cfd111909b578ecb5fee32c7bb9
Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 11:11:16 2026 +0100

    narrow the external_agents grant and stop announcing inert ones
    
    Four review findings on the executable-resolution work.
    
    discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing had the provider name in hand and still
    called DiscoverAndRegisterAlways, which globs every absolute $PATH entry
    and runs every entire-agent-* binary's info subcommand. The name comes
    from summary_generation.provider, honored from the COMMITTED
    .entire/settings.json, so one settings line in a pull request reached the
    full sweep on whoever pulled it. Route it through the named lookup that
    already existed for the --summarize-provider override, renamed from
    discoverDispatchSummaryProvider to discoverNamedSummaryProvider now that
    two paths share it.
    
    The non-interactive branches of resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider select a
    provider with no human involved (the only candidate, or the first of
    several on a headless run) and persisted the external_agents grant on the
    way through. That grant is repo-wide rather than scoped to the chosen
    provider. Gate it on summarySelectionOrigin so only a pick at the prompt
    flips it. The provider name is still persisted: it grants nothing by
    itself, and an auto-selected external provider keeps resolving through
    the named ungated lookup above, so nothing is lost at runtime.
    
    enableExternalAgentsLocally reported success for a write that cannot take
    effect. A tracked settings.local.json makes loadMergedSettings drop the
    whole local layer, and the usual rejection channel stays silent because
    enforceExternalAgentsTrust returns early on !s.ExternalAgents, which is
    the state a dropped layer produces. So the user saw "external agents are
    now enabled" over a grant nothing would ever read. Read the grant back
    and return whether it verified, preferring whichever rejection channel
    recorded something. Not an error: one committed file must not fail the
    command. persistSummaryProviderSelection is a fifth route to the same
    false claim and gets the same read-back.
    
    CLAUDE.md's new absolute-paths section read as a blanket rule while
    redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command is exec'd with no cmd.Dir and no
    absoluteness check. Name it as the deliberate exception, with the reason
    the trust gate makes it one.
    
    Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>

index df82978bd..66a72f475 100644
--- a/cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go
+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go
@@ -88,8 +88,11 @@ func resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) (*checkp
 
 	if s.SummaryGeneration != nil && s.SummaryGeneration.Provider != "" {
 		providerName := types.AgentName(s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
-		discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing(ctx, providerName)
+		blocked := discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing(ctx, providerName)
 		if err := ensureSummaryProviderPresent(ctx, providerName); err != nil {
+			if blocked {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w\nIf %s is an external plugin, enable external agents first: `entire agent` and pick it, or set \"external_agents\": true in .entire/settings.local.json", err, providerName)
+			}
 			return nil, err
 		}
 		return buildCheckpointSummaryProvider(providerName, s.SummaryGeneration.Model)
@@ -129,7 +132,9 @@ func resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) (*checkp
 }
 
 // discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing resolves a configured provider name that is
-// not registered yet.
+// not registered yet. It reports whether it declined to look because external
+// agents are not enabled, so the caller can say so rather than leaving the user
+// with "unknown summary provider" about a plugin that is installed.
 //
 // Named, never the sweep. The name arrives from summary_generation.provider,
 // which is honored from the COMMITTED .entire/settings.json, so routing it
@@ -139,15 +144,41 @@ func resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) (*checkp
 // lookup returns immediately for a built-in and touches exactly one binary
 // otherwise, so the ordinary case costs nothing either.
 //
-// The error is dropped for the reason discoverNamedExternalAgent gives: the
-// caller reports an unresolvable provider a few lines later, in terms of the
-// provider the user named rather than of the plugin protocol.
-func discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing(ctx context.Context, name types.AgentName) {
+// Named is not sufficient on its own, though, which is what the
+// external_agents check adds: one binary is still one binary, and the name
+// deciding WHICH one still came out of a tracked file. `{"summary_generation":
+// {"provider": "evil"}}` in a pull request is then enough to run
+// `entire-agent-evil info` on everyone who pulls it and runs `entire explain`,
+// with no prompt and no grant — the exact thing enforceExternalAgentsTrust
+// exists to prevent, reached by a path that never consults it.
+//
+// The gate lands only on the external case: the early return above covers every
+// registered agent, so a committed `"provider": "claude-code"` keeps working
+// with external agents off, as it must.
+//

+// and enforceExternalAgentsTrust. An enforceSummaryProviderTrust would let a
+// developer name an external provider in their own untracked
+// settings.local.json without granting the $PATH sweep, which is a real if
+// narrow want; it costs another settings-layer classification, another
+// rejection channel for `entire status` to surface, and another gate to keep in
+// step. It becomes worth writing when someone actually asks for that
+// combination -- until then, `entire agent` already offers the plugin, and
+// picking it there is what flips the grant.
+//
+// The discovery error is dropped for the reason discoverNamedExternalAgent
+// gives: the caller reports an unresolvable provider a few lines later, in
+// terms of the provider the user named rather than of the plugin protocol.
+func discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing(ctx context.Context, name types.AgentName) (blockedByExternalAgents bool) {
 	if _, err := getSummaryAgent(name); err == nil {
-		return
+		return false
+	}
+	if !settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled(ctx) {
+		return true
 	}
 	//nolint:errcheck,gosec // see doc comment: ensureSummaryProviderPresent reports it
 	discoverNamedSummaryProvider(ctx, name)
+	return false
 }
 
 // autoSelectSummaryProvider builds a provider for an auto-selected candidate

commit eb8d27c09d0cfef89fae5b1736c2ffa47531fb21
Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 16:28:35 2026 +0100

    fix(git): validate branch names in the three helpers that skipped it
    
    BranchExistsOnRemote passes the name to `git ls-remote` and to go-git,
    BranchExistsLocally to go-git, and CheckoutBranch to `git checkout` behind
    nothing but a leading-dash guard. All three take names from CLI input or
    from a trail's branch field.
    
    The dash guard was the narrowest part of the problem: `git checkout` also
    reads `--`, a pathspec, and `@{-1}`. ValidateBranchName covers those, and
    it still admits an object id, so CheckoutBranch's documented "or commit"
    behaviour survives even though no caller uses it.
    
    Validating both existence helpers rather than only the remote one keeps
    their answers symmetric: they are called side by side on the same name,
    and "invalid" from one with "no such branch" from the other is worse than
    either.
    
    Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1PGJD97M4X8P0H3VSM2683T

commit f61b0c0b97353af59f450dbf8f66df9c6e13be08
Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 16:34:02 2026 +0100

    fix(userdirs): one absolute-override rule for every per-user directory
    
    requireAbsPluginParent applied the rule to ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR,
    XDG_DATA_HOME and LOCALAPPDATA; ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR and XDG_CACHE_HOME had
    no such check, and they redirect the directories holding the login tokens
    and the discovery caches. A relative value there resolves against the
    working directory, so the same environment names a different directory in
    every process — usually one inside whatever repository the command ran
    from.
    
    Lift the rule into userdirs.RequireAbsoluteOverride, which both reach
    (userdirs cannot import cli, so calling the plugin copy was not an
    option), and delete the plugin-local one.
    
    Config() and Cache() keep their string signatures, so the refusal lands at
    the roots instead: userdirs' own resolveUserRoot, which checks before
    creating anything, plus contexts.configRoot and discovery.cacheFile.root,
    which open their own roots on the directory they are handed. Those two
    called filepath.Abs on it first, which turned the exact mistake being
    guarded against into a plausible-looking absolute path.
    
    Falling back to the platform default was considered and rejected: for the
    config directory that default is the developer's real ~/.config/entire,
    and silently substituting it for a mistyped override — a test harness's,
    say — is worse than failing.
    
    Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit b39971518495704213ba9053ba3c437063581f1d
Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Fri Sep 4 16:35:12 2026 +0100

    test(agent): ratchet the unconfined transcript-read set
    
    Entire's rooting is knowingly asymmetric around transcripts: every
    WriteSession goes through SessionStore, which rejects a SessionRef outside
    the agent's session directory, while the reads have no boundary at all —
    and the read is what pulls transcript content into a checkpoint.
    
    Closing that needs RepoPath on HookInput, a change to the external-plugin
    protocol rather than a refactor, which is exactly the kind of work that
    stalls while the count quietly climbs: a new agent integration copies the
    nearest existing one, so the shape spreads by imitation and nobody
    re-derives whether it is safe. CLAUDE.md said "eight"; there are fourteen.
    
    Pin the per-file count and fail the build in both directions — on growth,
    and on a stale entry, since the count is the only record of how much of
    the gap is left.
    
    Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>

content.text:
All six substantive commits are still needed. I checked each against `78a655db4` by looking at whether the gap it closes still exists in main:

| Commit | Still needed? | Evidence in main |
|---|---|---|
| `fix(hooks)` rooted hooks dir | **Yes** | `strategy/hooks.go` still does bare `os.ReadFile`/`os.WriteFile` on `filepath.Join(hooksDir, hook)` at 6 call sites (lines 237, 442, 482, 488, 511). Main's `0ec5743b3` scoped hook *ownership*, not the path handling. |
| `fix(explain)` gate on `external_agents` | **Yes** — complementary, not duplicate | See below. |
| `fix(git)` branch-name validation | **Yes** | `CheckoutBranch` still has only `strings.HasPrefix(ref, "-")`; `BranchExistsOnRemote`/`Locally` still validate nothing. |
| `fix(userdirs)` absolute-override rule | **Yes** | No `IsAbs` check anywhere in main's `userdirs.go` — `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` are still unchecked. |
| `test(agent)` transcript-read ratchet | **Yes** | No such guard file exists in main. |
| `test(versioncheck)` literal pin | **Yes** | No such test in main. |

Plus `refactor: self-review polish`, which only exists to touch up the five above.

**The one worth a closer look is `fix(explain)`.** Main landed `f237f08b8` ("narrow the external_agents grant…") which addresses the *same* vulnerability — it replaced the full `$PATH` sweep with a named lookup. That could easily look like the branch commit is now redundant. It isn't: the branch commit was already written on top of that fix (it edits main's `discoverNamedSummaryProvider` and quotes its "Named, never the sweep" comment), and it closes the residual hole main explicitly left open. I traced it in the current main:

`summary_generation.provider` (honored from **committed** `.entire/settings.json`) → `discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing` → `discoverNamedSummaryProvider` → `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` → `registerExternalAgent` → `New(ctx, binPath)`, which executes the binary's `info` subcommand.

So on main today, one line in a pull request still runs `entire-agent-<name> info` on everyone who pulls it and runs `entire explain` — no prompt, no grant, `enforceExternalAgentsTrust` never consulted. Narrowing the sweep to a named lookup bounded it to one binary; it didn't make it zero. The branch commit adds the `settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled` gate that does.

**One caveat about staleness rather than redundancy.** 106 commits landed in main since the branch point, and two of them changed the ground under this work in ways the rebase had to reconcile — that's what the two conflicts were. The versioncheck one mattered: main split `realRunInstaller` per-platform and made the Windows fallback *deliberately* interpolate the install dir, so the commit's "every command is a literal" invariant is no longer true cross-platform. I rescoped the test and the docs to unix (where `sh -c` actually runs) rather than porting it as written — otherwise it would have been a test that fails on Windows asserting an invariant main had already, correctly, abandoned there.

Verified after rebase: `go build ./...` and `GOOS=windows go build ./...` clean, `cli`/`agent`/`versioncheck`/`strategy`/`osroot`/`entireclient` tests pass, `mise run lint` reports 0 issues.

message.content:
Here's some feedback for the changes:

- entire disable can never finish if the hooks directory is a symlink. Uninstall only deletes Entire's own files, but it now refuses outright and exits non-zero — forever, until the user edits git config by hand. The refusal should be install-only.
- An unreadable pre-existing hook gets destroyed, silently. If Entire can't read a hook (bad perms), it doesn't classify it as foreign → no backup → the new atomic rename overwrites it anyway (rename only needs the directory writable). The old code failed loudly and left the file alone.
- Auto-selected external summary provider breaks on the next run. Entire auto-picks an external plugin, saves it, but doesn't grant external_agents — so the next entire explain can't resolve the provider it just wrote. The comment at explain_summary_provider.go:350 still claims this works.
4. The relative-directory check fires too late. ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR=foo still creates the directory and its lock file before erroring — the exact mistake it's meant to prevent.
5. The token store slipped the net. It's a fourth path into the config tree and still accepts a relative dir, so bearer tokens can land inside the user's repo. The new doc comment says this can't happen.
6. The remedy text prints broken commands — git config core.hooksPath its target, or a relative path git will resolve from the wrong place.

Minor

7. The new ratchet test has two holes — counts lines not matches, and can't see untracked files.
8. CheckoutBranch's comment overstates what it fixes. Pathspecs still get through (git checkout README.md silently discards edits and returns success). Adding -- fixes it.

Let's discuss how each will be resolved. Also, from all the symlink blockers, which ones may make sense to provide an opt-in scape hatch via settings.local.json?

content.text:
All eight confirmed. Two are worse than reported, and two are regressions this branch introduced rather than pre-existing gaps.

## Verification notes first

**#1 is not limited to `disable` — it's a full lockout.** `gitHookStateInHooksDir` returns `GitHooksAbsent` when `hooksRoot` fails, so `EnsureSetup` sees "not installed" → calls `ReinstallGitHooks` → `InstallGitHook` → hard error. `EnsureSetup` is called from `lifecycle.go:600`, the agent hook path. So a symlinked hooks directory doesn't just block uninstall; it fails every turn of session capture, and `enable`, and `doctor --fix`. The user can't disable *and* can't use it.

**#2 is a regression, and I reproduced the mechanism:**
```
old (os.WriteFile, O_TRUNC):  PermissionError: [Errno 13] ... 'pre-push'   ← loud, file intact
new (temp + rename):          rename OK → content replaced                 ← silent destruction
```
`ReadFileNoFollow` returning EACCES matches neither arm of the `foreign` expression, so it falls through as "not foreign" → no backup → `writeHookFile`'s own read also fails → straight to `WriteFileAtomicIn`. The same hole exists in reverse in `RemoveGitHook`: `hookExists := readErr == nil || errors.Is(readErr, ErrSymlinkedPath)` classifies an unreadable hook as *absent*, so a `.pre-entire` backup gets renamed over it.

**#3 is a regression too, and the stale comment is the smoking gun.** Before commit `3c466aac4`, `explain_summary_provider.go:350` was true. Our gate made it false. The loop: auto-select picks an external plugin (via the ungated always-variant), `persistSummaryProviderSelection` writes `provider: X` but not the grant because `origin != selectionByUser`, next run takes the configured-provider branch, `discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing` refuses, error. Entire writes a config that breaks itself.

**#8, empirically:**
```
git check-ref-format --branch README.md   → exit 0        (valid branch name)
git checkout README.md                     → exit 0, edits gone, "Updated 1 path from the index"
git checkout README.md --                  → exit 128, "fatal: invalid reference", edits intact
git checkout feature --                    → works;  git checkout <sha> -- → works (detached)
```
So `--` closes it without costing the documented "or commit" behaviour.

## Proposed resolutions

| # | Fix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Split `hooksRoot` into `hooksRootForInstall` (refuses a link) and `hooksRootForRemoval` (resolves it, anchors at the target). Point `RemoveGitHook` **and** `gitHookStateInHooksDir` at the removal variant. | Detection must move too, or the lockout survives the uninstall fix. |
| 2 | Classify positively — no fall-through. `existingErr == nil` → marker check; `ErrSymlinkedPath` → foreign; `fs.ErrNotExist` → absent; **anything else → hard error, write nothing.** Same switch in `RemoveGitHook` before restoring a backup. | This is the `.entire` scan's "identify each condition positively, no `else` branch" discipline, which CLAUDE.md already argues for. |
| 3 | Don't persist a setting that can't take effect: when `origin == selectionAutomatic` and the pick is external and the grant isn't held, skip the write and print "using X for this run; `entire agent` to make it stick". | See below — this is a real decision. |
| 4 | `contexts.FilePath` and the tokenstore call `RequireAbsoluteOverride` **before** `EnsurePrivateDir`. The check has to precede every `MkdirAll`, not just the root open. | |
| 5 | Route `FileBackendPath()`'s no-env case through a checked resolver, and drop the `filepath.Abs` laundering in `fileStore.dir()` for that case. Correct the `Config()` doc comment — it names two consumers and there are three. | |
| 6 | Resolve the link to an absolute path for the remedy (`filepath.EvalSymlinks`, not `os.Readlink` — a relative target is relative to the link's parent, not the worktree). When it can't be resolved, print a remedy that doesn't contain a placeholder: point at `git config --show-origin --get-all core.hooksPath` instead of emitting `git config core.hooksPath its target`. | |
| 7 | `-o` instead of `-c` (counts matches, not lines), plus `--untracked`. | |
| 8 | Append `--` in `CheckoutBranch`, and cut the comment's claim back to what validation actually covers. | Keep `ValidateBranchName` — it still earns its place for `@{-1}` and newlines. |

Two of these are worth more than a table row:

**#3.** Three options, and I'd take the third. (a) Grant `external_agents` on auto-selection — no; main's `f237f08b8` deliberately removed exactly that, and flipping a repo-wide exec grant with no human in the loop is the thing the trust gate exists to stop. (b) A per-provider grant (`enforceSummaryProviderTrust`) — this is the design our own doc comment considered and rejected as not-yet-worth-it; it's the *right* long-term answer if someone wants "name an external provider locally without granting the sweep", but it's a fourth trust gate with its own rejection channel for `status` to surface. (c) Don't write the broken config. The run still works (the agent is registered in-process from the always-variant discovery), and the *next* run re-discovers and auto-selects the same provider — so behaviour is unchanged except that nothing lies on disk. It's also the principle main already established in `f237f08b8` for `enableExternalAgentsLocally`: don't report success for a write that cannot take effect. Same bug class, same fix.

**#7.** Worth noting `--untracked` still honours `.gitignore`, which is what we want — a generated or vendored file shouldn't trip the ratchet. And with `-o` the counts in `unconfinedTranscriptReads` need re-deriving; they may not all be the same numbers.

## The escape hatch

I'd add exactly one, and it isn't for the blocker in this branch.

**Yes: the agent hook-config directories** (`.claude`, `.cursor`, `.gemini`, `.codex`, `.pi`, `.factory`). This is a real, common setup — dotfile managers (chezmoi, stow, yadm) symlink `.claude` into the repo, and the population that runs coding agents is precisely the population that does this. CLAUDE.md already concedes the use case is legitimate and offers `git rm --cached` + `.gitignore` as the workaround; that workaround is fine for the *file* but doesn't help someone whose whole `.claude` is managed. Shape it as a **list of paths the user vouches for**, not a boolean:

```json
{ "allow_symlinked_agent_dirs": [".claude"] }
```

Constraints that make it safe: `settings.local.json` only, behind `classifyLocalSettingsDeep` (the same untracked-in-index-**and**-HEAD gate as `external_agents` and OPF `command`) — a repo that ships "follow my symlinks" is the entire attack; a list rather than a flag, so the user names what they set up rather than disabling the class; a rejection channel surfaced by `entire status`; and `doctor` reports `following .claude -> /home/u/dotfiles/claude (allowed by settings.local.json)` so it stays visible rather than silent. Note this only needs to cover the **directory** — with `.claude` linked, `.claude/settings.json` is an ordinary file inside it and everything works. A symlinked config *file* stays refused, because allowing it needs more than a permission bit: the write is a rename, which would replace the user's link with a regular file.

**No: the git hooks directory (#1's blocker).** Git already has the escape hatch — `core.hooksPath` can name the target directly, which says the same thing without the indirection. Adding a setting would be a second way to express something git expresses natively. Fix the remedy text (#6) and the uninstall/detection lockout (#1) and there's nothing left to want.

**No: `.entire`, its entries, and the settings files.** Two reasons. First, `.entire` holds the redaction settings that decide what may be committed and pushed; "follow this link to decide what your transcripts leak" is not a knob to offer. Second, and decisive: the hatch would live in `settings.local.json`, which is one of the files being protected — a symlinked `settings.local.json` granting "follow symlinked settings files" is self-authorizing. There's no non-circular place to put it. The genuine want here (relocating `.entire/logs` and `.entire/tmp` out of the worktree, which CLAUDE.md names as a deferred non-goal) wants a settings key naming a directory that the code can validate and root properly — not a symlink the code follows blindly.

Two things I'd like your call on before I start: whether **#3** goes with (c) don't-persist or you want the per-provider grant built now, and whether the escape hatch is in scope for this branch or a follow-up. My inclination is (c) and follow-up — these eight are bug fixes, and the hatch is a feature with a trust-gate surface of its own. Fixing #1 removes the acute "stuck forever" pain that would otherwise argue for rushing it.

75		// agent integration is a new file: the guard would pass on the developer's

88		}

95			}

103		}

106		}

108		for file, count := range found {

110			if !listed {

113					"cannot be confined yet, add the file to unconfinedTranscriptReads with the reason — "+

// Absent rather than Current: a symlinked hook is not one we wrote, so reporting
// it as installed would leave it in place forever. Absent is what sends
// EnsureSetup to InstallGitHook, which backs it up and chains to it.
func TestCheckGitHookState_SymlinkedHookIsNotOurs(t *testing.T) {
	_, hooksDir := initHooksTestRepo(t)

	_, err := InstallGitHook(context.Background(), true, false)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, GitHooksCurrent, CheckGitHookState(context.Background()))

	hookPath := filepath.Join(hooksDir, "post-commit")
	ours, err := os.ReadFile(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	elsewhere := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "post-commit")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(elsewhere, ours, 0o700))
	require.NoError(t, os.Remove(hookPath))
	if err := os.Symlink(elsewhere, hookPath); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlink not supported: %v", err)
	}

	assert.Equal(t, GitHooksAbsent, CheckGitHookState(context.Background()),
		"a link to a file carrying our marker is still not a hook we installed")
}

// Removal must not follow a link either: the hook at that path is not ours, so
// it stays, and it blocks a backup from being restored over it.
func TestRemoveGitHook_LeavesSymlinkedForeignHook(t *testing.T) {
	_, hooksDir := initHooksTestRepo(t)

	_, err := InstallGitHook(context.Background(), true, false)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	hookPath := filepath.Join(hooksDir, "post-commit")
	require.NoError(t, os.Remove(hookPath))
	elsewhere := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "post-commit")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(elsewhere, []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"), 0o700))
	if err := os.Symlink(elsewhere, hookPath); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlink not supported: %v", err)
	}

	_, err = RemoveGitHook(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	info, err := os.Lstat(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err, "a foreign hook must survive removal")
	assert.NotZero(t, info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink)
}

**`external.Agent.run` refuses a non-absolute `binaryPath` before spawning.**
`run` sets `cmd.Dir` to the worktree root and `os/exec` resolves a relative
`Path` against `Dir`, so the file `registerExternalAgent` statted is not
necessarily the file that executes. The check lives at the exec, not at the
caller, so it also covers the exported `New`.

**A per-user directory override must be absolute**, and there is one
implementation of that rule: `userdirs.RequireAbsoluteOverride`. A relative
value resolves against the working directory, so the same environment names a
different directory in every process — usually one inside whatever repository
the command ran from. It covers all three trees an override can redirect:
`pluginParentDir` (`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `LOCALAPPDATA` — a
tree whose `bin` subdirectory `main.go` prepends to `$PATH`), and the config and
cache directories (`ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`), which hold the login
tokens and the discovery caches. Leaving it to `osroot` (which refuses a
relative root open) and to `main.go`'s `PATH` restore was not wrong, but each
backstop answers a question of its own, two layers from where this one is
decided.

directory that default is the developer's REAL `~/.config/entire`, so quietly
substituting it for a test harness's mistyped override is worse than an error.
`userdirs.Config()`/`Cache()` cannot report — too many callers only want the
string — so the refusal lands at every root opened over those directories:
`userdirs`' own (`resolveUserRoot`, which checks *before* creating anything),
plus `contexts.configRoot` and `discovery.cacheFile.root`, which open their own.

content.text:
All eight are fixed, with tests. Unit (10,797) and integration (562) suites pass, lint is clean, both platforms build.

## What changed

**#1 — install-only refusal.** Split into `hooksRootForInstall` (refuses a link) and `hooksRootForRemoval` (resolves it, anchors on the target). `RemoveGitHook` **and** `gitHookStateInHooksDir` now use the removal variant. The detection half mattered as much as the uninstall half: it reported `GitHooksAbsent`, which sent `EnsureSetup` → `InstallGitHook` → the same refusal, on every agent turn. Justification for the asymmetry is at the function: removal only deletes marker-bearing files and renames back backups Entire itself made, so following the link costs nothing install-time refusal was protecting.

**#2 — no silent destruction.** `classifyExistingHook` identifies absent/ours/foreign positively and returns an error for anything else; install refuses to write, removal treats it as present-and-not-ours (so no backup is renamed over it) and warns rather than erroring, so uninstall still finishes. I reproduced the mechanism first — truncating write → `PermissionError`, temp+rename → succeeds and destroys — and the doc comment records it.

**#3 — (c), don't persist.** An auto-selected external provider without the grant returns `errSelectionNotPersistable`; the run completes and prints how to make it stick. Verified the loop is actually closed with a round-trip test (auto-select → save → resolve again), and confirmed it fails against the old behaviour.

**#4/#5 — the check moved ahead of the mkdir, and the token store joined.** `contexts.FilePath` and `withCacheFileLock` check before `EnsurePrivateDir`/`MkdirAll`. 3	import (

14	)
15	
16	// Vouched agent directories: the one place a symlink Entire would otherwise
17	// refuse is followed on purpose.
18	//
19	// The refusal these opt out of is real and stays the default. A working tree
20	// arrives by clone, so a symlink at `.claude` can be something the REPOSITORY
21	// chose, and `entire enable` would then create directories and write JSON
22	// through it to wherever it points. Nothing about the link says which of those
23	// two it is.
24	//
25	// What tells them apart is not the link. It is who said the link is fine, and
26	// where they said it: settings.AllowSymlinkedAgentDirs is honored only from an
27	// untracked, index-and-HEAD-verified .entire/settings.local.json, the same gate
28	// that guards the OPF command and external_agents. A repository cannot put a
29	// path in that list, so following one is always this developer's own decision
30	// about their own machine.
31	//
32	// It exists because the setup is ordinary rather than exotic: dotfile managers
33	// (chezmoi, stow, yadm) symlink `.claude` into a repository, and the people
34	// running coding agents are the people who use those. Before this, the only
35	// answer was to stop managing the directory that way.
36	//
37	// Deliberately NOT extended to `.entire`, to the settings files, or to the git
38	// hooks directory:
39	//
40	//   - `.entire` holds the redaction settings that decide what may be committed
41	//     and pushed. "Follow this link to decide what your transcripts leak" is
42	//     not a knob worth having.
43	//   - A settings file is where the grant itself would live, so a symlinked
44	//     settings.local.json vouching for symlinked settings files would authorize
45	//     itself. There is no non-circular place to put that permission.
46	//   - The git hooks directory already has this escape hatch, and git owns it:
47	//     `git config core.hooksPath <target>` says the same thing without the
48	//     link. A second spelling would be ours to keep in step for no gain.
49	var (
50		vouchedMu   sync.RWMutex
51		vouchedDirs []string
52	)
53	
54	// SetVouchedSymlinkedDirs installs the set of worktree-relative agent
55	// directories whose symlinks may be followed, replacing any previous set, and
56	// returns the entries it refused.
57	//
58	// Refusal is by NAME, against the directories actually derivable from the
59	// agents' own hook-config paths (see VouchableSymlinkedDirs). That is what keeps
60	// the list from becoming a general "follow symlinks" switch: `.entire`,
61	// `.git/hooks`, and anything else that is not an agent's config directory are
62	// not spellable here at all, whoever is doing the spelling.
63	//
64	// The zero value vouches for nothing, so a caller that never configures a
65	// policy gets the strict behaviour. That direction is deliberate: forgetting
66	// this call costs a refusal the user can act on, where the opposite default
67	// would silently follow links nobody approved.
68	func SetVouchedSymlinkedDirs(dirs []string) (rejected []string) {
69		vouchable := VouchableSymlinkedDirs()
70		accepted := make([]string, 0, len(dirs))
71		for _, d := range dirs {
72			clean := path.Clean(filepath.ToSlash(strings.TrimSpace(d)))
73			clean = strings.TrimSuffix(clean, "/")
74			if clean == "" || !slices.Contains(vouchable, clean) {
75				rejected = append(rejected, d)
76				continue
77			}
78			if !slices.Contains(accepted, clean) {
79				accepted = append(accepted, clean)
80			}
81		}
82	
83		vouchedMu.Lock()
84		vouchedDirs = accepted
85		vouchedMu.Unlock()
86		return rejected
87	}
88	
89	// VouchedSymlinkedDirs returns the accepted set, for doctor and status to
90	// report what is being followed rather than leaving it invisible.
91	func VouchedSymlinkedDirs() []string {
92		vouchedMu.RLock()
93		defer vouchedMu.RUnlock()
94		return slices.Clone(vouchedDirs)
95	}
96	
97	// VouchableSymlinkedDirs is every worktree-relative directory a user may vouch
98	// for: each directory component of every agent's hook-config path.
99	//
100	// Derived from AllHookConfigRelPaths rather than hand-kept, for the reason
101	// doctor's agentSymlinkCheckPaths gives: a hand-kept list is how `.pi/extensions`
102	// and `.opencode/plugins` came to be missed. Deriving it also means the set can
103	// only ever name agent config directories, which is the property that makes the
104	// name check a boundary rather than a formality.
105	func VouchableSymlinkedDirs() []string {
106		var out []string
107		for _, relPath := range AllHookConfigRelPaths() {
108			dir := path.Dir(filepath.ToSlash(relPath))
109			for dir != "." && dir != "/" && dir != "" {
110				if !slices.Contains(out, dir) {
111					out = append(out, dir)
112				}
113				dir = path.Dir(dir)
114			}
115		}
116		slices.Sort(out)
117		return out
118	}
119	
120	// isVouched reports whether a worktree-relative directory has been vouched for.
121	func isVouched(dir string) bool {
122		vouchedMu.RLock()
123		defer vouchedMu.RUnlock()
124		return slices.Contains(vouchedDirs, dir)
125	}
126	
127	// AnchorWorktreePath resolves the directory to anchor a root on for a
128	// worktree-relative path, following a vouched symlinked agent directory and
129	// returning the remaining name inside that directory.
130	//
131	// Walks the path's directory components outside in. A component that is not a
132	// symlink stays a NAME inside the current base, which is what keeps the strict
133	// open below able to refuse it; a component that IS a symlink is followed only
134	// when its accumulated worktree-relative path was vouched for, and re-anchors
135	// the walk on the resolved target. An unvouched link is left in the name on
136	// purpose, so the caller's own MkdirAllNoSymlink / LstatNoSymlinks refuses it
137	// and says which component, exactly as before.
138	//
139	// followed names the links that were resolved, so callers can report them. It
140	// is normally empty.
141	//
142	// Exported because the skill scaffolds (writeManagedScaffold) write under the
143	// same agent directories and must reach the same place. A vouched `.claude`
144	// that hook installation follows but scaffolding does not would leave `entire
145	// enable` half-applied, with files in two directories.
146	func AnchorWorktreePath(worktreeRoot, relPath string) (baseDir, name string, followed []string, err error) {
147		segments := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(relPath), "/")
148		baseDir = worktreeRoot
149		onDisk := worktreeRoot
150		vouchName := ""
151		start := 0
152	
153		for i := 0; i < len(segments)-1; i++ {
154			onDisk = filepath.Join(onDisk, segments[i])
155			vouchName = path.Join(vouchName, segments[i])
156	
157			info, lerr := os.Lstat(onDisk)
158			if lerr != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
159				continue
160			}
161			if !isVouched(vouchName) {
162				continue
163			}
164			resolved, rerr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(onDisk)
165			if rerr != nil {
166				// A vouched but unresolvable link is an error rather than a silent
167				// fallback to the strict path: the user said to follow this one, and
168				// "we could not" is a different answer from "we would not".
169				return "", "", nil, &VouchedDirError{Dir: vouchName, Err: rerr}
170			}
171			followed = append(followed, vouchName)
172			baseDir = resolved
173			onDisk = resolved
174			start = i + 1
175		}
176		return baseDir, strings.Join(segments[start:], "/"), followed, nil
177	}
178

182	// The single place the anchor for a worktree-relative agent path is chosen, so
183	// the hook configs and the skill scaffolds cannot drift onto different bases.
184	// The two bases it can return are both trusted: the worktree root, which a
185	// resolver produced, and a vouched directory's resolved target, which the user

content.text:
The escape hatch is in, and everything passes: 10,811 unit + 562 integration + 120 E2E canary tests, lint clean, both platforms build.

## What it looks like

```json
// .entire/settings.local.json  (untracked, verified against index AND HEAD)
{ "allow_symlinked_agent_dirs": [".claude"] }
```

With that, a dotfile-managed `.claude` works: hook configs and skill scaffolds are written at the link's target. Without it, nothing changes — the default vouches for nothing.

## The three properties that make it a hatch and not a hole

**A list, not a boolean.** A flag would disable the class; naming a path is the user saying which arrangement is theirs.

**Two independent boundaries, both required.** `enforceSymlinkedAgentDirsTrust` answers *may this file grant anything* — same untracked-and-verified gate as the OPF command and `external_agents`, because a repository that could both ship the link and vouch for it is the entire attack. Then `agent.SetVouchedSymlinkedDirs` answers *is this path one an agent config lives under*, so `.entire` and `.git/hooks` are unspellable **even from a verified local file**. There's a test for exactly that combination.

**Pinned, not derived** — and this is the one worth flagging, because my first version got it wrong. I derived the vouchable set from `agent.AllHookConfigRelPaths()`, which reads well and is wrong twice: that registry is **mutable at runtime** (external plugins register into it), so a plugin could widen what a user may be persuaded to vouch for; and it's **empty in any binary that hasn't imported the agent packages**, so the set silently collapsed depending on the caller's import graph. The settings tests surfaced the second one. It's now a pinned list plus a structural `neverVouchable` rule, with `TestVouchableDirsMatchTheBuiltInAgents` in the `cli` package (where every built-in agent *is* registered) failing on drift in both directions — verified by deleting `.codex` and by adding `.ssh`.

Scope: vouching `.claude` does not vouch for links inside it. The scaffolds go through the same anchor, or `enable` half-applies across two directories. A vouched-but-unresolvable link is an error, not a quiet fall back to refusing. `status` prints what's followed and what was rejected; `doctor` reports it under FOLLOWING SYMLINKS instead of as a fault.

Excluded as discussed: `.entire`, the settings files (circular — a symlinked `settings.local.json` vouching for symlinked settings files authorizes itself), and the git hooks directory (git's own `core.hooksPath` already is the hatch).

## One thing I found on the way

The **root-base guard had the same untracked-file hole as finding #7** — `git grep` without `--untracked`. It reported my new `vouched_dirs.go` as a *stale allowlist entry*, i.e. it told me to delete the entry that legitimises the new root. That's the more misleading direction of the same bug. Fixed both call sites in `rootbase_guard_test.go`. Worth knowing that the class had a second instance; there may be other `git grep` guards I haven't looked at.

1	// Package gitenv isolates test git invocations from the host's git config.
2	// It deliberately imports nothing from this repo so that internal tests of
3	// low-level packages (e.g. gitrepo, which testutil itself imports) can use it
4	// without an import cycle; testutil re-exports it for everyone else.
5	package gitenv
6	
7	import (
8		"os"
9		"os/exec"
10		"strings"
11		"sync"
12		"testing"
13	)
14	
15	// emptyConfigPath returns the path to a config file suitable for use as
16	// GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM. We use a real file instead of
17	// os.DevNull because git on Windows cannot open NUL as a config file.
18	//
19	// The file is not strictly empty: it pins background maintenance off so that
20	// no detached `git gc`/`git maintenance` process lingers after a test holding
21	// an open handle on the temp repo's .git/objects. Such a lingering process
22	// races t.TempDir()'s deferred RemoveAll and fails the test with
23	// "directory not empty" (see COR-394). Suppressing it centrally keeps every
24	// git-shelling test that uses Isolated/IsolateProcess safe.
25	var emptyConfig string
26	var emptyConfigOnce sync.Once
27	
28	// EnvHermetic, when set to a non-empty value, makes emptyConfigPath append
29	// per-host HTTP proxy config that routes git HTTPS transport to real external
30	// hosts (github.com, gitlab.com) through an unroutable loopback proxy. Any test
31	// whose git commands accidentally dial those hosts then fails fast (connection
32	// refused at 127.0.0.1:1) instead of reaching the network or prompting for
33	// credentials. It is opt-in per test process — the integration TestMain sets it
34	// — so unit test packages that don't set it are unaffected. Because
35	// Isolated strips all inherited GIT_CONFIG_* env, this config must live in
36	// the file GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points at (this one), not in GIT_CONFIG_* env
37	// entries.
38	//
39	// A dead proxy (not url.insteadOf) is used deliberately: insteadOf rewrites the
40	// effective URL that git reports on read, which breaks production code that
41	// resolves the origin URL to detect the forge (e.g. `entire trail`). The proxy
42	// blocks transport only, leaving the configured URL string intact, and is scoped
43	// per host so loopback (127.0.0.1) test servers are never proxied.
44	//
45	// Regression class: tests accidentally hitting live github.com / the macOS
46	// keychain (#1463, 53bc37a88).
47	const EnvHermetic = "ENTIRE_TEST_GIT_HERMETIC"
48	
49	// hermeticGitConfig routes HTTPS transport to real external hosts through a dead
50	// loopback proxy. Loopback test servers (127.0.0.1) and file:// / bare-path
51	// remotes are not proxied, so the in-process HTTPS git server still works. Only
52	// HTTPS is covered — the accidental-dial regression class is HTTPS fetches; SSH
53	// (git@…) to a real host fails on its own without credentials.
54	const hermeticGitConfig = "[http \"https://github.com/\"]\n" +
55		"\tproxy = http://127.0.0.1:1\n" +
56		"[http \"https://gitlab.com/\"]\n" +
57		"\tproxy = http://127.0.0.1:1\n"
58	
59	func emptyConfigPath() string {
60		emptyConfigOnce.Do(func() {
61			f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "git-isolation-config-*")
62			if err != nil {
63				panic("create git isolation config: " + err.Error())
64			}
65			content := "[gc]\n\tauto = 0\n\tautoDetach = false\n[maintenance]\n\tauto = false\n[fetch]\n\twriteCommitGraph = false\n"
66			if os.Getenv(EnvHermetic) != "" {
67				content += hermeticGitConfig
68			}
69			_, err = f.WriteString(content)
70			if err != nil {
71				panic("write git isolation config: " + err.Error())
72			}
73			if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
74				panic("close git isolation config: " + err.Error())
75			}
76			emptyConfig = f.Name()
77		})
78		return emptyConfig
79	}
80	
81	// Isolated returns os.Environ() with git isolation variables set.
82	// This prevents user/system git config (global gitignore, aliases, etc.) from
83	// affecting test behavior. Use this for any exec.Command that runs git or the
84	// CLI binary in integration tests.
85	//
86	// See https://git-scm.com/docs/git#Documentation/git.txt-GITCONFIGGLOBAL
87	//
88	// Every inherited GIT_CONFIG_* entry is filtered out — including
89	// GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and the indexed KEY_/VALUE_ pairs that can inject
90	// `git -c` overrides — so our explicit isolation overrides take effect
91	// regardless of parent env.
92	func Isolated() []string {
93		env := os.Environ()
94		filtered := make([]string, 0, len(env)+2)
95		for _, e := range env {
96			if isGitConfigEnv(e) {
97				continue
98			}
99			filtered = append(filtered, e)
100		}
101		return append(filtered,
102			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="+emptyConfigPath(), // Isolate from user's global git config (e.g. global gitignore)
103			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM="+emptyConfigPath(), // Isolate from system git config
104		)
105	}
106	
107	// IsolateProcess applies the same git config isolation to the current
108	// process. Use this in tests that exercise production code paths which invoke
109	// git with os.Environ(). All inherited GIT_CONFIG_* variables are cleared
110	// before the isolation overrides are set, so values such as
111	// GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS or indexed KEY_/VALUE_ overrides cannot leak into
112	// child git invocations.
113	func IsolateProcess(t *testing.T) {
114		t.Helper()
115	
116		for _, e := range os.Environ() {
117			key, _, ok := strings.Cut(e, "=")
118			if !ok {
119				continue
120			}
121			if strings.HasPrefix(key, "GIT_CONFIG_") {
122				t.Setenv(key, "")
123			}
124		}
125	
126		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", emptyConfigPath())
127		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM", emptyConfigPath())
128		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM", "1")
129		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_COUNT", "0")
130	}
131	
132	// IsolateMain is IsolateProcess for a TestMain, which has no *testing.T to
133	// restore through: the isolation is set process-wide for the whole run via
134	// os.Setenv and inherited by every spawned binary and git hook. Inherited
135	// GIT_CONFIG_* overrides are neutralized (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 disables the
136	// indexed KEY_/VALUE_ pairs) rather than unset.
137	func IsolateMain() {
138		for k, v := range map[string]string{
139			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL":     emptyConfigPath(),
140			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM":     emptyConfigPath(),
141			"GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM":   "1",
142			"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT":      "0",
143			"GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS": "",
144		} {
145			if err := os.Setenv(k, v); err != nil {
146				panic("set " + k + ": " + err.Error())
147			}
148		}
149	}
150	
151	// Run runs one git command in dir with an isolated git config, failing the
152	// test on error and returning combined output.
153	func Run(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) string {
154		t.Helper()
155		cmd := exec.Command("git", args...) //nolint:noctx // test helper, no context needed
156		cmd.Dir = dir
157		cmd.Env = Isolated()
158		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
159		if err != nil {
160			t.Fatalf("git %v in %q: %v\n%s", args, dir, err, out)
161		}
162		return string(out)
163	}
164	
165	// EmptyConfigOverrides returns the GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL / GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM
166	// settings Isolated applies, for callers that build their own environment on a
167	// different base and still want the caller's git config kept out.
168	func EmptyConfigOverrides() []string {
169		return []string{
170			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=" + emptyConfigPath(),
171			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=" + emptyConfigPath(),
172		}
173	}
174	
175	func isGitConfigEnv(e string) bool {
176		return strings.HasPrefix(e, "GIT_CONFIG_")
177	}

p='CLAUDE.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='''### Code Duplication Prevention'''
new='''### Source-Level Guard Tests

Four tests scan this repo's own source with `git grep` to enforce an invariant
the compiler cannot: `TestRootBasesAreTrusted` (root bases are trusted paths),
`TestTranscriptReadsOnlyShrink` (the unconfined transcript-read ratchet),
`TestGitStatusCallSitesPassNoOptionalLocks`, and
`TestAllHookConfigRelPaths_CoversEveryWorktreeConfigAgent`.

**They all go through `testutil.GitGrepGuard`, which owns three flags.** Each was
missing from at least one guard, and the same one was missing from three:

- `--untracked`. `git grep` searches the INDEX. Every one of these guards has
  "someone just added a file" as its subject, so the file it most needs to see is
  the one not yet staged. Two failure shapes were worse than a miss: the
  hook-config guard compares two sets built from the same blind grep, so a new
  agent package calling `OpenHookConfig` without declaring `HookConfigRelPath`
  was absent from both and the comparison *passed*; and the root-base guard's
  staleness half reported a just-added entry as STALE, telling the author to
  delete the entry that legitimised their new root.
- `--no-color`. `color.ui`/`color.grep` set to `always` colorizes into a pipe and
  the escapes land in the **filename** field. True of `-l` too, which looks
  immune. Guards then either misparse (read as staleness, #2248) or compare
  garbage to garbage while their "did we match anything" assertion still passes.
- Repo-selector scrubbing. Git exports `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` to hooks and
  they outrank `cmd.Dir`, so a `go test` under a hook or `git rebase --exec`
  scanned a different repository. `RunGit`'s isolation does **not** cover this:
  it filters `GIT_CONFIG_*` only.

Two rules for writing one:

- **A pathspec restricted to `*.go`, so an unparseable path can be fatal.** The
  `git status` guard passed a bare `cmd internal`, which also matched testdata
  `.jsonl` and a `.md`, so its non-`.go` branch had to `continue` — and that
  skip was the only thing between colorized output and a guard that silently
  checked nothing.
- **Fail on zero matches.** A detection pattern that goes stale otherwise passes
  forever. `GitGrepGuard` does this itself; the `checked == 0` tallies are the
  second half of the same idea.

### Code Duplication Prevention'''
assert anchor in s; s=s.replace(anchor,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")
PY

content.text:
Found five guards, not four. All fixed and consolidated.

## The four `git grep` guards

| Guard | `--untracked` | `--no-color` | env scrub |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TestRootBasesAreTrusted` | missing (I'd fixed) | had it | **missing** |
| `TestTranscriptReadsOnlyShrink` | missing (I'd fixed) | had it | **missing** |
| `TestAllHookConfigRelPaths_...` | **missing** | **missing** | had it |
| `TestGitStatusCallSitesPassNoOptionalLocks` | **missing** | **missing** | **missing** |

So it wasn't one hole in two guards — it was three holes spread unevenly across four, with no guard having all three. Each is now `testutil.GitGrepGuard`, which owns all three and carries the reasoning once.

Evidence for each, measured rather than argued:

- **`--untracked`**: `git grep -l` for `agent.OpenHookConfig` returns 0 matches for an unstaged file, 1 with the flag. The hook-config guard is the worst instance — it compares *two sets built from the same blind grep*, so a new agent package calling `OpenHookConfig` without declaring `HookConfigRelPath` was absent from both sides and the comparison **passed**. I verified it now fails, and that the `git status` guard now catches an unguarded call in an unstaged file.
- **`--no-color`**: `git grep -l` colorizes filenames too — `\e[35mpkg/a.go\e[m` — which I'd assumed was `-n`-only. In the hook-config guard that breaks the `_test.go` suffix check (leaking test files into both sets) while `require.NotEmpty` still passes. All four now pass under a hostile local `color.ui=always`.
- **env scrub**: confirmed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` outrank `cmd.Dir` against a decoy repo. Notably `testutil.RunGit`'s isolation does **not** cover this — `gitenv.Isolated()` filters `GIT_CONFIG_*` only — so the `git status` guard inherited a false sense of safety from using it. All four now pass under a decoy `GIT_DIR`.

One extra fix the migration forced: the `git status` guard's pathspec was a bare `cmd internal`, which also matched testdata `.jsonl` and a `.md`, so its non-`.go` branch had to `continue` — and that skip was the only thing standing between colorized output and a guard that silently checked nothing. Narrowed to `*.go`, so an unparseable path is now fatal.

## The fifth guard

`TestGitMetadataTraversalHasCanonicalOwner` (`gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go`) — an AST-based audit of `git rev-parse` call sites. I didn't find it by searching for `git grep` because it doesn't use one; it found *me*, failing on `GitGrepGuardRepoRoot`'s `--show-toplevel`. Added with a documented reason. Worth noting it walks the filesystem rather than the index, so it has none of the three holes — which is an argument for that style.

Full suite: 10,811 unit + 562 integration + 120 canary, lint clean, both platforms build.

One judgement call to flag: I consolidated into a shared helper rather than fixing four copies in place, on the grounds that finding the same bug in three of four is the drift the repo's own comments warn about. That touched shared test infra (a new `EmptyConfigOverrides` in `gitenv`), which is more surface than a one-word fix per guard. If you'd rather keep the guards independent, the flags are the load-bearing part and revert cleanly to local changes.

content.text:
Commit A is staged. Here's the full three-commit plan — **not committed yet**, so you can unlock your GPG agent first.

## Commit A — review findings (staged now)

15 files, +703/−88. Findings #1–#6 and #8.

```
fix(hooks,settings): address review findings on the hardening commits

Seven findings, of which two are regressions the preceding commits
introduced rather than gaps they left.

The git hook directory's symlink refusal was shared by install, removal
and detection, so a symlinked hooks directory could not be uninstalled
past -- RemoveGitHook is the only uninstall path -- while
gitHookStateInHooksDir reported GitHooksAbsent, sending EnsureSetup to
InstallGitHook and failing every agent turn on the same refusal. Split
hooksRoot into ForInstall (refuses) and ForRemoval (resolves), and point
removal and detection at the latter: both act only on files Entire wrote,
so following the link costs nothing the install-time refusal protected.

A hook that could not be READ was classified "not foreign", so it got no
backup, and the write is an atomic rename, which needs no permission on
the target at all. An unreadable hook was silently destroyed where the
in-place write it replaced failed loudly with EACCES. classifyExistingHook
now identifies absent/ours/foreign positively and refuses to write on
anything else; removal treats the same case as present-and-not-ours so a
backup is not renamed over it either.

Gating discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing on external_agents made an
auto-selected external provider unresolvable on the next run, while
persistSummaryProviderSelection still wrote it down -- Entire breaking
itself with its own write, with the stale comment still claiming it
worked. Persist nothing in that case: the run in progress has the agent
registered already, and the next run re-selects the same provider.

The relative-directory refusal fired at the root open, which is the READ,
several steps after contexts.FilePath and withCacheFileLock had created
./<value> and dropped a .lock in it. Check before every MkdirAll, not
merely before every root open. The token store is a fourth consumer of
userdirs.Config() with no root to check at, since it anchors on the
dirname of a path the caller may have named; it now calls
ConfigDirChecked and carries the error, so ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR=foo no
longer puts bearer tokens inside the repository.

The symlinked-hooks-directory remedy printed commands that do not work: a
relative readlink target that git resolves from elsewhere, or the literal
`git config core.hooksPath its target`. Resolve it, and when it cannot be
resolved print no command at all.

CheckoutBranch validated the ref and then let git read it as a pathspec.
`check-ref-format --branch test.txt` exits 0, and `git checkout test.txt`
in a repo with no such branch restores the file from the index, discarding
the user's edits, and exits 0. Validation cannot fix this in principle --
a filename is often a legal branch name -- so pass a trailing `--`.
```

## Commit B — the escape hatch

`agent/vouched_dirs.go` + test (new), `settings/symlinked_agent_dirs_trust.go` + test (new), `agent/hook_config_file.go`, `settings/settings.go`, `setup_managed_scaffold.go` + test, `setup_search_skill.go`, `setup_agent_help_skill.go`, `status.go`, `doctor.go` (FOLLOWING SYMLINKS), `osroot/rootbase_guard_test.go` (allowlist entry only), `CLAUDE.md`.

```
feat(agent): allow vouched symlinked agent config directories

A dotfile-managed .claude (chezmoi, stow, yadm) is an ordinary setup among
exactly the people who run coding agents, and the only answer Entire had
was to stop managing it that way.

allow_symlinked_agent_dirs in .entire/settings.local.json names
worktree-relative agent config directories whose symlinks are followed,
anchoring the root on the resolved target. Three properties keep it a
hatch rather than a hole. It is a list, not a boolean: a flag disables the
class, where naming a path says which arrangement is the user's. It has
two independent boundaries -- the same untracked-and-verified gate as the
OPF command and external_agents decides whether the FILE may grant, and a
name check decides whether the PATH is one an agent config lives under, so
.entire and .git/hooks are unspellable even from a verified local file.
And the vouchable set is pinned rather than derived from
AllHookConfigRelPaths: that registry is mutable at runtime, so deriving
would let a plugin widen what a user can be persuaded to vouch for, and it
is empty in a binary that has not imported the agent packages, so the set
collapsed depending on the caller's import graph.
TestVouchableDirsMatchTheBuiltInAgents catches drift both ways.

Vouching for a directory does not vouch for links inside it. The skill
scaffolds go through the same anchor, or enable half-applies across two
directories. A vouched but unresolvable link is an error, not a quiet fall
back to refusing. status prints what is followed and what was rejected,
and doctor reports it as FOLLOWING SYMLINKS rather than as a fault.
```

## Commit C — the git grep guards (separable for its own PR)

`testutil/gitgrep.go` (new), `testutil/gitenv/gitenv.go`, `osroot/rootbase_guard_test.go`, `agent/transcript_read_guard_test.go`, `agent_hook_config_guard_test.go`, `gitrepo/gitstatus_guard_test.go`, `gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go`, `CLAUDE.md`.

```
test: fix three holes in the git grep source guards

Four tests scan this repo's own source with `git grep`. Three flags matter
and no guard had all three; the same one was missing from three of them.

--untracked, because git grep searches the INDEX. Every one of these
guards has "someone just added a file" as its subject, so the file it most
needs to see is the one not yet staged. Two shapes were worse than a miss:
the hook-config guard compares two sets built from the same blind grep, so
a new agent package calling OpenHookConfig without declaring
HookConfigRelPath was absent from both and the comparison passed; and the
root-base guard's staleness half reported a just-added entry as STALE,
telling the author to delete the entry legitimising their new root.

--no-color, because color.ui set to `always` colorizes into a pipe and the
escapes land in the filename field. True of -l too, which looks immune.
Guards then either misparse (read as staleness, #2248) or compare garbage
to garbage while their "did we match anything" assertion still passes.

Repo-selector scrubbing, because GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE outrank cmd.Dir, so
a `go test` under a hook scanned another repository. RunGit's isolation
does not cover this: it filters GIT_CONFIG_* only.

Consolidated into testutil.GitGrepGuard so the reasoning lives once.
Also: the ratchet counted `git grep -c` LINES rather than matches, so a
second read on an existing line was invisible; the git status guard's bare
`cmd internal` pathspec matched testdata fixtures, so its non-.go branch
had to skip rather than fail, which was the only thing between colorized
output and a guard checking nothing; and metadata_guard_test.go gets an
audited-query entry for the new helper.
```
